source: docs/dataset-spec.md §3 (time_colloquial: periods and minute words) and docs/harness-spec.md §8 (the time lexicon)
notes: A linguistic resource for the normaliser, not benchmark text. Entries are folded before matching (Arabic folding, ASCII digits, casefold), so «تلاتة» and «تلاته» are one entry.

hours: the clock-hour words 1-12 in Egyptian (cardinals), MSA (feminine ordinals after «الساعة»), Arabizi (house spellings) and English. An hour word only counts as a time next to «الساعة»/'at', a minute word or a period word, so «اتنين» alone is never a time.

minutes_after: minute words that follow the hour (spec table: «وخمسة» :05 ... «إلا خمسة» :55); a negative value counts back from the hour («خمسة إلا ربع» = 4:45). Written with and without the space after «و».
minutes_before: English minute phrases that precede the hour ('half past six' = 6:30, 'quarter to five' = 4:45).

periods: the spec's windows («الصبح» 06-12, «الضهر» 12-15, «بعد الضهر» 15-17, «العصر» 15:30-17:30, «المغرب» about 18, «بليل/بالليل/العشا» 19-24) plus the a.m./p.m. markers; `shift` decides the 24-hour clock (am: as written; noon: 12 stays 12, 1-3 add 12; pm: add 12 below 12). The single letters «ص»/«م» count only right after a time ('5:00 م').
markers: words that announce a clock time before a bare hour («الساعة ٥», 'at 5', el sa3a 5).
Without a period the hour is resolved from the opening hours when given (the policy block states them): the reading that falls inside the hours wins, the written one if both or neither do.
